description: Runs the APS exception-resolution pipeline for one uploaded exception report: parse the Excel workbook, normalize rows into planning issues, classify each exception, gather related supply / demand / due-date facts from SyteLine (read-only), apply the deterministic APS rules engine, then bounded agent steps for root-cause, recommendation, and grounded SyteLine procedure steps, and finally record a versioned snapshot of the issue. The run ends at record-snapshot: 'Planner Executes' is a human run boundary, not a flow step — the planner takes the SyteLine steps (via aps.getIssue or the run view), executes them in SyteLine, uploads a new exception report, then starts aps-exception-verify. The platform has no pause/await primitive and we do not fake one.

exceptionReportDocumentId.description: Document id of the uploaded APS exception report workbook (from the documents service)

issueId.description: Planning issue id; pass "" (empty string) to create a new issue on first analysis

site.description: SyteLine site the report and all fact lookups apply to

name: aps-exception-analysis

issueId.description: The issue id (newly created by aps.recordSnapshot when the input issueId was "")

snapshotId.description: The snapshot id recorded for this analysis run

steps.prompt:
You are classifying SyteLine APS exception-report rows for a human planner. APS (Advanced Planning and Scheduling) allocates on-hand and planned supply to demands by priority, with a supply-usage tolerance; it can switch supply between demands, generating Move In / Move Out exception messages. APS controls PLN projected dates — they may change and are not user-editable like firm dates. Status lifecycle matters: customer-order lines are Planned / Ordered / Open; purchase orders are Planned / Ordered / Open; jobs are Firm / Released / Complete; PLN is a planned-order record created by APS — firming it converts it into a real job or PO. Available = on-hand minus allocated can go negative; with non-negative on-hand, negative available means allocated demand exceeds physical supply.

Classify each issue row below into exactly one category:
- LATE_SUPPLY: a scheduled supply (PO receipt, job completion) is projected after the demand's due date.
- MATERIAL_SHORTAGE: on-hand plus scheduled receipts cannot cover the demand (projected available goes negative).
- MOVE_IN_MOVE_OUT: an APS reschedule exception — supply exists but its projected date is earlier or later than the demand needs (Move In = needed sooner; Move Out = supply arrives earlier than needed).
- PLN_DATE_DRIFT: APS moved a PLN order's projected date relative to the prior report.
- UNCOVERED_DEMAND: demand with no linked supply at all.
- OVERSTOCK: excess supply beyond the demand horizon.
- DATA_ISSUE: the row reflects bad or missing data (bad dates, unknown item, stale status, unexplained negative on-hand).

Severity: critical = a customer commit is at risk now; high = a miss within this planning cycle; medium = actionable soon; low = informational.

Issues (JSON): {{steps.normalize-rows.output.issues}}

Return JSON matching the output schema: one classification per issue row, in row order.

title: APS exception report analysis: parse, classify, root-cause, recommend
